headline: Data centre operators in Australia face regulatory and community pushback, particularly around residential proximity and energy supply, prompting moves toward self-generation via solar.
reasoning: Huljich acknowledges that data centre development faces pushback from local governments and communities, especially when proposed sites are near residential areas or schools. He notes Centuria specifically targets industrial areas or precincts already hosting data centres to mitigate this risk. Energy supply is identified as another hot-button issue, with most operators exploring on-site solar and other forms of self-generation to address concerns.
quote: You've got to be very careful where you're going with these these sites. Um, you know, if you're going into an area where it's close to residential schools, things like that. That's where you are seeing a lot of pushback. Um, look, our facilities are in areas that are industrial areas or areas that have other data centers in them. Um, so it's something you've got to be aware of. Obviously, the energy issues, the other one that's a hot topic at the moment. Um, so I think most operators in the space are looking at how can they supply their own energy through solar and other forms as well.

headline: Centuria sees office property valuations stabilising after Covid-driven sentiment-led weakness, with some assets sold above book
reasoning: Huljich notes that real estate valuations across most sectors have stabilised over the past 18 months. Industrial has been the standout, with consistent valuation uplift each six-month period. Office suffered the most from negative post-Covid sentiment but has now stabilised, and Centuria has successfully sold some office assets at meaningful premiums to book value, indicating the sector's recovery is progressing.
quote: It depends on the sector. We've definitely seen over the last 18 months stabilise. We've had some sectors like industrial have been very strong the whole way through, and we've seen uplift in every six month period for quite a while. Um, office was probably the one that, because of sentiment, has struggled the most since Covid, but we've definitely seen that stabilised and we've even sold some assets, you know, with quite a bit of premium above the book values as well. So most valuations have stabilised or are going the right way.

headline: Centuria comfortable with its Bathla Group exposure in its $2.5bn real estate credit book, describing risk as not material
reasoning: Centuria's credit fund has exposure to six Bathla Group projects; five are fully completed, titled and selling down at valuation with minimal residual risk. The sixth is a construction project in its final weeks before titling, with good pre-sales and sales tracking at valuation. Huljich explains the firm benefits from cross-collateralisation across all facilities, providing an equity buffer across the pool. He acknowledges larger risks exist for lenders holding half-finished or barely-started projects but is confident Centuria is well protected given its experienced 530-person property team.
quote: We've said we've got exposure to six projects of theirs. Five of them are fully complete, titled Selling Down. So very little risk there. You know, we've leant on a valuation. We're seeing the sales come through at valuation and they'll just be sold down and we'll realize our funds. We have one construction project that is in the final weeks of completion and titling, and that will be sold down as well... We've got cross collateralization. So all the facilities are linked. So if there's any equity in any of the other deals that can be brought into any other particular deal. So I think we're very well protected. There's a good equity buffer.
